A bitcoin is simply a unit of measurement that represents a token. The token is the reward given for the miners efforts. Miners are a decentralized data center stored nowhere, for they are everywhere in the world and thus cannot lose power and go offline as easily.

The blockchain is a massive spreadsheet. Every time I send you a Bitcoin, and you send one to me, we broadcast the "public" side of that transaction to the entire network. The miners are the horsepower that relays our transaction to each-other, and vise versa. The miners are seeking a large, randomly generated number in the billions to billions character lengths long, and they randomly generate numbers in the billions of lengths long, billions of times a second, as a byproduct of their carrying the network of our transactions.

The blockchain is an algorithm that is designed, in the case of Bitcoin, to keep the "update" of the ledger to a set interval - 10 minutes approximately. The number of miners online represents a level of "number hunting" represented as a global hash rate, that could be looked at like the horsepower of a car. If you turbocharge the car, it has more horepower. If you add more miners, the network hash rate increases, if you remove miners, the network hash rate decreases. The algorithm's job is to manipulate the length of the randomly generated number relatively proportionate to the number of miners, and their global hash rate, so that the next number is found arouind 10 minutes in - thereby updating the blockchain itself.

Every time a new Bitcoin is found, two things happen:

  1. The miner who finds the random number is considered the "winner" of the easter egg hunt, and given a reward in the form of Bitcoin. This work can be shared among a large group of miners combining their effort into a "pool", and receiving a proportion of the reward - if I am 10% of a pool that discovers a Bitcoin, I get 10% of a bitcoin, and maybe that pool fines a Bitcoin every few hours, or every few days.
  2. The miner that wins broadcasts their overall network update of every transaction in the past 10 minutes to the entire network. Since the network is consensus driven, as long as 51%+ of all other miners acknowledge the same ledger, then the block is codified in the ledger as valid transactions and the entire ledger verifies and moves on to the next block. This means if you make a transaction it takes 10 minutes to verify and then it is permanent.
